care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child - my son Alex. I live here in the UK and I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's good to know you have a son named Alex and that you live in the UK.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few more questions.

How old is Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's a teenager - I think he's around 16 or 17, somewhere in that range. To be honest, I'd need to double-check his exact age, but he's definitely between 15 and 19.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is in his mid-to-late teens, his eligibility may depend on whether he's in education or training.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure what counts as "non-advanced education" - could you explain what that means? I want to make sure I give you the right answer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course! I'm happy to clarify that for you.

"Non-advanced education" typically refers to education up to and including A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQ Level 3, or similar qualifications. It does NOT include university degrees or higher education courses.

So this would include things like:
- GCSEs
- A-levels or AS-levels
- Scottish Highers
- T-levels
- NVQs up to Level 3
- Similar school or college courses

University courses (like a bachelor's degree) would be considered "advanced education" and wouldn't count.

Is Alex currently studying any of these types of qualifications full-time at school or college?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Ah, I see. No, he's not in any of those courses. He's not studying at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex is not currently in education or training.

Just to confirm - is Alex under 16 years old, or is he 16 or over?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 16 or over - like I mentioned, he's somewhere between 15 and 19, but I'm pretty sure he's at least 16.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. 

So to summarize what you've told me about Alex:
- He is 16 or over
- He is not currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training

Based on the Child Benefit rules, Child Benefit can be claimed for children under 16, or for young people aged 16-19 if they are in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 16 or over and is not in approved education or training, I'm afraid you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

Is there anything else about Alex's situation I should know, or do you have any other children you'd like to ask about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. No, Alex is my only child, so that's all I needed to know. Thank you for explaining that to me - I appreciate your help in clearing that up.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you.

To summarize: Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex because he is 16 or over and is not currently in full-time approved education or training. Child Benefit can only be claimed for children under 16, or for young people aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if he decides to go back into education or approved training - you may become eligible at that point, so it would be worth revisiting then.

If you have any other questions, feel free to ask. Best wishes to you and Alex!
